render_decomposition.note: render stage = 1 forward (recon) + 4 forwards (central-diff Jacobian of pixel positions for derivative-matching loss). native_GT uses only 1 forward/iter.

dominant_cost: backward (5.56 ms/iter, 68.1%) then render (2.11 ms/iter, 25.9%). Per-tile problem is tiny (<=256 px, ~1.2k gaussians/tile); GPU kernel-launch + autograd-graph overhead dominates. Adam also needs far more iters than L-BFGS-B to converge on this smooth least-squares problem.
OBSERVED: backward 68.1%, render 25.9%, opt 3.5%, loss 2.6% of native per-iter time.
INFERENCE: native GPU per-tile optimization is launch-overhead-bound and optimizer-inefficient (Adam vs quasi-Newton) for this workload size.
NOT_MEASURED: batched (all-tiles-simultaneous) native optimization; larger tile / multi-view joint optimization; CUDA-graph capture to remove launch overhead.
